# debian/common/packages.txt - installed on every card, whatever the
# desktop. Only what is needed and proven on the tablet. One package per
# line, then "#" and what it is. Installed without Recommends.
#
# Base system
systemd-sysv            # systemd as the init system
udev                    # device manager
dbus                    # system message bus
dbus-user-session       # message bus for the user's session
libpam-systemd          # login sessions (logind) - needed by sway
systemd-resolved        # name resolution (DNS)
systemd-timesyncd       # clock from the network
kmod                    # load kernel modules
sudo                    # run commands as root
locales                 # languages
tzdata                  # time zones
console-setup           # console font and keyboard
console-data            # console keyboard maps
kbd                     # console tools (setfont, setvtrgb, ...)
apt-utils               # package tools
debian-archive-keyring  # Debian's signing keys
ca-certificates         # certificates for https
linux-sysctl-defaults   # lets normal users ping
polkitd                 # permissions for system services (rotation, host name)
# Network
wpasupplicant           # Wi-Fi login
iw                      # Wi-Fi information
wireless-regdb          # Wi-Fi channels allowed per country
iproute2                # ip: network addresses and routes
iputils-ping            # ping
openssh-server          # log in from another computer (ssh)
avahi-daemon            # <host>.local names on the local network
libnss-mdns             # find other computers' .local names
curl                    # download from the web
wget                    # download from the web
# Bluetooth, sound, volume keys
bluez                   # Bluetooth (bluetoothctl)
alsa-utils              # sound tools (alsamixer, aplay, amixer)
triggerhappy            # volume keys and headphone jack
# Cameras
v4l-utils               # camera tools (v4l2-ctl, media-ctl) - used by cam-snap
python3                 # Python - used by cam-snap's raw2png.py
python3-numpy           # numbers in Python - used by raw2png.py
# Hardware checks
i2c-tools               # read chips on the I2C buses
usbutils                # lsusb
evtest                  # show input events (keys, touch)
fbset                   # framebuffer information
# Files and disks
e2fsprogs               # ext4 tools
dosfstools              # FAT tools
fdisk                   # partition tool
parted                  # partition tool
rsync                   # copy and synchronise files
file                    # tell a file's type
unzip                   # unpack .zip files
util-linux-extra        # more system tools (hwclock, ...)
# Shell
bash-completion         # Tab completion in bash
less                    # page through text
nano                    # simple text editor
vim-tiny                # vi text editor
micro                   # text editor with familiar keys (Ctrl+S, Ctrl+Q)
mc                      # Midnight Commander, file manager in the console
htop                    # running programs, CPU and memory
procps                  # ps, top, free
psmisc                  # killall, pstree
man-db                  # manual pages (man)
manpages                # the system's manual pages
fonts-terminus          # Terminus font
